name: awkwardness
quote: Um, maybe we could, er, dance a little?
description: Social tension from making a minor social mistake or not knowing what to do or say next.
perceptions: I made a minor social mistake.
I'm not sure what to do next.
I'm concerned about my social image.
examples: Physical or verbal stumbling in front of others.

guidance.description: You can work on being less awkward by connecting with empathy, practicing social interactions, and learning to read social cues. We’ll dive into these practical tips, but first, let’s step back and look at this nerve-wracking topic from a broader POV.

comparisons.description: 'Awkwardness' is more about not knowing what to do or say in a certain situation while 'social anxiety' is frequent awkwardness and the fear of being judged. Awkwardness may be a part of an overall social anxiety, or it could just be a short pause in the conversation after someone says something unusual.

variations.name: awkwardness in others
variations.description: Social tension from someone else making a minor social mistake or not knowing what to do or say next.
perceptions: Someone made a minor social mistake.
examples: Pause in the conversation after someone says something personal.

guidance.description: This article will help with awkward situations. Instead of getting caught by awkwardness like a deer in headlights, understand how you can master these situations instead.

commentaries.quote: Awkwardness is a more real disadvantage than it is generally thought to be; it often occasions ridicule, it always lessens dignity.
Awkwardness is such a gold mine for comedy.
Sometimes there is such beauty in awkwardness.
God may forgive sins, he said, but awkwardness has no forgiveness in heaven or earth.
